review_basis: inputs/path_glossary_bundle.json: concept contexts, prerequisites, blocked_future_concepts and required facts
tile_lessons/*.json: assembled learner text, media summaries and bridges, and remediation

coverage.text_review: Exhaustive, including nested visual text, code examples and annotations, step ledes, takeaway and up-next text, and assembled media labels, summaries and bridges.
coverage.interaction_review: Reviewed sampled prompts, options or classification items, supplied editable workspace text, constraints, and learner feedback. Sample spans every tile and emphasizes code examples with possible future-concept scaffolding. No deterministic gates were rerun.

issues.evidence: The handler-order example includes with open("missing-example.txt", "r") as source: before either resource management or file modes is taught.
issues.description: These are incidental scaffolding, not a needs-to-understand dependency: the learner can follow the missing-file failure and first-matching-handler rule without understanding file closure or mode semantics. Still, unfamiliar syntax may distract from the intended handler-order distinction.
issues.exact_fix: Optionally insert this prose immediately before the code walkthrough: 'The try body attempts to open and read a file. For this step, focus only on which except handler runs; the file-opening and resource-management syntax is supplied background, not part of the task.'

conclusions: No reviewed text or sampled interaction requires understanding a blocked future concept.

Within-tile sequencing was evaluated at concept level: exception matching is already a required fact of exception propagation; specific-before-broad handling later elaborates it rather than making earlier matching questions leakage.
Function objects, Path construction and built-in exception use do not require understanding the later classes-and-instances concept.

The traceback capture implementation in learn_python.tile.057_059.s08 is explicitly instructor-supplied and unchanged; the learner reads displayed source and report evidence rather than needing to understand exception attributes, introspection or dynamic execution internals.

Up-next titles are passing mentions. The specific-handler media's undefined-name example illustrates a misleading broad recovery, without requiring the later diagnostic classification concept. Neither is blocking leakage.
